name: Whitechapel Gallery
summary: A public art gallery on Whitechapel High Street, founded in 1901, in a historic building that includes the former Whitechapel Public Library and has nine exhibition spaces.

music.notes: Exhibitions and displays alongside screenings, talks, workshops and livestreamed events.

crowd: Its own website says its participation programmes put local communities first.

accessibility.notes: Common Rooms, a free space to sit and read, are reached by lift or stairs. Sensory tools are kept at the ground-floor information desk, and Visitor Services can help plan a visit.

cost.notes: The main entrance and displays are free, with one ticketed exhibition each season (standard £16.50 when checked). Pay what you can during Thursday evening Whitechapel Lates. Members get free entry.

evidence.quote: the Gallery was founded in 1901 to enrich the cultural offer for the people of East London
Our historic building, which incorporates the former Whitechapel Public Library, houses nine exhibition spaces
Our Participation programmes prioritise our local communities
Main Entrance is free and gives access to an inspiring and dynamic programme of exhibitions, displays, screenings, talks and events.
Visitors of all ages are invited into this participatory workshop
Livestream – Art Futures: Platforms for Dissent with Tania Bruguera and Pankaj Mishra
There are chairs, sofas and books available in Common Rooms, accessible via lift or stairs.
Fidget spinners and other sensory tools can be found at the Information Desk on the ground floor.
For assistance with planning your visit around the Gallery, please contact the Visitor Services team
We offer free displays and one ticketed exhibition each season.
Pay What You Can entry to all exhibitions during Whitechapel Lates: every Thursday 6–9pm
Becoming a member supports us year round and offers a range of benefits from free entry
